title: When Tools Silently Lie: Evaluating and Mitigating Blind Compliance in Tool-Augmented Data Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.37153v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool-augmented data agents rely on tool outputs for analytical decisions. Yet successful execution can return plausible but incorrect evidence, requiring agents to decide whether to trust or verify it. Understanding this failure requires examining both the evidence obtained through checking and the answer ultimately adopted. We introduce ToxicBench to measure checking and adoption under numerical, label, schema, and retrieval errors, pairing clean and poisoned observations over fixed source data. In the 118-task GPT evaluation across three adapters, poisoning lowers task success by 26 to 39 percentage points. Ordinary retries help under one-shot poisoning, whereas repeated poisoning reveals wrong-answer adoption after checking. Controls on three public tables isolate how supplied evidence affects recovery. After freezing the scorer, we compare its judgments with human annotations on 200 trajectories, finding 96% task-success agreement. H

translated_title: 当工具悄然撒谎：评估与缓解工具增强数据代理中的盲从行为
translated_abstract: 工具增强的数据代理依赖工具输出来做出分析决策。然而，成功执行的工具可能返回看似合理但实际错误的证据，这就要求代理决定是信任还是验证这些证据。理解这种失败需要同时考察通过检查获得的证据以及最终采纳的答案。我们提出了ToxicBench，用于测量在数值错误、标签错误、模式错误和检索错误情况下的检查与采纳行为，在固定源数据上配对干净与被污染的观测结果。在跨三个适配器的118个任务的GPT评估中，污染使任务成功率降低26至39个百分点。普通重试在单次污染情况下有帮助，而重复污染则揭示了代理在检查之后仍采纳错误答案的现象。在三个公开数据表上的对照实验分离出了所提供证据如何影响恢复效果。在冻结评分器之后，我们将其判断与200条轨迹上的人工标注进行比较，发现任务成功率判断的一致性达到96%。
tldr: 本文提出ToxicBench基准，用于评估与缓解工具增强数据代理在工具返回看似合理却错误的证据时的盲从行为，发现数据污染可使任务成功率下降26至39个百分点，并揭示了代理在检查证据后仍采纳错误答案的失效模式。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ToxicBench, a benchmark for evaluating and mitigating blind compliance in tool-augmented data agents when tools return plausible but incorrect evidence, showing that poisoning reduces task success by 26–39 percentage points and exposing agents' failure to adopt correct answers even after checking.
